Under the Hood

"Can this even work?" Yes — with boring, well-supported browser tech. And here's the idea it's built to serve.

The winning formula

⚡ Speed

One gesture. Space, type three letters, any table in your library is on screen. Keyboard-first, because at the table your eyes are on the players, not the menu.

⚖ Zero context-loss

What you summon floats over the open adventure — it never navigates away. Pin a whole board of references; it's saved per adventure and waiting when you return.

📚 One reach

Every book, one shelf. One party that follows you. One dice log for the night. Own more — the whole thing gets richer. Free, offline, yours.

✅
It works. A shell page loads each Keeper in its own isolated frame, indexes their tables into the Summon, and saves everything to the browser's own database. Runs offline at the table. Ships as one downloadable file, or an installable app.

The architecture

Gnasher's Grimoire — the shell (this app)
The Summon
One fuzzy index of every table across every book, built from each Keeper's manifest. The command palette searches it.
The Board + Party + Dice
Floating cards, one roster with portraits, one session roll-log. The DM surface that sits above whatever's running.
Shelf + Switcher
The library. Click a cover, it mounts that Keeper. Swap freely; split two side by side.
▤ Keeper (frame)
Each adventure runs unmodified in its own isolated frame — its own DM tools, dice, secrets intact. Nothing to rebuild.
▤ Keeper B (frame)
A second book loads on demand for split view, sandboxed so scripts never collide.
💾 The Binder (IndexedDB)
Books, boards, party, portraits, roll-log. Export the whole thing as one .keeper file to back up or move devices.
Frames talk to the shell through a tiny message bridge — that's how a table gets pulled out and floated over what's running.

The contract that makes it snap together

Every Keeper is cloned from one engine template. We add one small block to it — a manifest: title, cover, and the book's tables with tags (wilderness, urban, weather, loot…). The Summon reads those manifests. Ship a new book → it appears on the shelf and its tables show up in the Summon automatically. Books already out there get read straight off the page — nothing has to be rebuilt.

The one real wrinkle (and the fix)

⚠ Save data across isolated frames

A book in a sandboxed frame can't always keep its own save reliably. The fix: the shell owns all save data centrally and hands each Keeper its state on open (the engine already has export/import — we just drive it). One binder, one source of truth. The only piece that needs a small touch to the engine template.

Why it's a moat, not just a tool

A PDF dies in a downloads folder. Give away this deck free and every LIDM adventure someone buys snaps into a living thing that gets better the more they own — a deeper Summon, cross-book tables, one party through all of it. It's the DM's second screen, and it only fills up with your books.

About

Gnasher's Grimoire™ · Version ? · © 2026 Long Island Dungeon Master. 'Gnasher's Grimoire', 'Adventure Keepers', and the .keeper format are marks of Long Island Dungeon Master.

Free tool. Runs offline; your books stay yours. Get more books at longislanddungeonmaster.com/keepers.

The Theater: your players pair Gnasher's Satchel, its free companion, straight to this screen. No server, no accounts; the pairing code is the connection, and a same-room mode works with no internet at all.

Found a bug, or something that made no sense? Tell me about it — the Grimoire writes up the technical details, you read them, and you send it. Nothing is ever transmitted by the app itself.

The Chronicle: the binder's campaign memory. Seal how each chapter of a campaign ended and every later chapter opens already knowing what your table did; a short Chronicle Code carries the same story to any table, no binder needed.

Tomes: shelve your own PDFs beside your Keepers. They are stored in this browser only and never leave it. They stay out of .keeper backups and the Drive Binder, so keep the PDF files themselves too.

🐛 Report a problem

Something broken, confusing, or just wrong? Tell me what happened and the Grimoire will write up the technical details for you.

What gets sent — read it, it is the whole report

The Grimoire never sends this anywhere. There is no telemetry and no reporting service; you copy or send it yourself. Everything the app added is counts and status — no book text, no character names, no table code, no whispers, no notes. Your description is included exactly as you type it, so leave out anything you would not want to share. (“Email it” hands the report to your own mail app, which may be webmail. If a table is open, the Grimoire keeps talking to the code service for pairing, as it always does — that is unrelated to this report.)

Paste it wherever suits you: frank@longislanddungeonmaster.com. Bugs, wishes and “this bit made no sense” are all equally welcome.

How the Theater works
1. Link the table. Tap Open the table by code and read the code aloud (something like EMBER-42). Each player types it into their Satchel (the wax seal, top left) and taps Join. No internet at the venue? Tap Same room first, or share your phone's hotspot; the + Invite by paste button trades the link as copied text instead.
2. Run the fight. Nothing extra to do: your combat tracker drives every paired Satchel. Each player sees the order, and a YOUR TURN banner when it's them.
3. Handouts. Title, text or image, Push text or Push image. Pick a name in the To row to whisper it to one player alone; everyone else never sees it.
4. Resting seats. A player's phone dozing off shows their seat as resting. Keep playing; whatever you push is held and delivered the moment their screen wakes. Their Satchel rejoins by itself.
5. The code sticks. A saved table keeps the same code, so your players type it once and it still works next week. Reload this page mid-session and the table reopens on its own, seats and all, with nobody typing anything. Only Change the code makes them retype.
Players start at longislanddungeonmaster.com/satchel.
